flawed_step: Step 2: convergence of X_n to X in distribution does not imply joint convergence of (X_n,X) to (X,X).
counterexample: Let Ω={0,1}² with the uniform probability measure. Define X(a,b)=a and X_n(a,b)=b for every n. Each X_n and X has the Bernoulli(1/2) distribution, so X_n converges to X in distribution. However, P(|X_n-X|>1/2)=P(a≠b)=1/2 for every n, so convergence in probability fails.
assessment_summary:
1. Assume X_n converges to X in distribution. — JUSTIFIED: This is precisely the hypothesis.
2. Assert that (X_n,X) converges in distribution to (X,X). — NOT JUSTIFIED: Convergence of the marginal distributions of X_n gives no control over the joint dependence between X_n and X; this is the first failing step in the natural proof attempt.
3. From Step 2, apply the continuous function (u,v)↦|u−v| to infer |X_n−X| converges in distribution to 0. — NOT JUSTIFIED AS USED: The continuous-mapping inference would be valid if Step 2 were true, but Step 2 does not follow from the hypothesis.
4. Infer P(|X_n−X|>ε)→0 for every ε>0. — NOT JUSTIFIED AS A CONCLUSION FROM THE PREMISE: It would follow from Step 3 because a nonnegative random variable converging in distribution to the constant 0 converges to 0 in probability, but Step 3 is unsupported.
5. To determine whether the failed proof reflects a false statement, take Ω={0,1}² uniformly, set X(a,b)=a, and set X_n(a,b)=b for every n. — JUSTIFIED: These are real random variables on one common probability space.
6. Each X_n has exactly the same distribution as X, namely Bernoulli(1/2), so F_{X_n}(t)=F_X(t) for every t and hence X_n converges to X in distribution. — JUSTIFIED: Equality of the distribution functions directly satisfies the stated definition.
7. For ε=1/2, P(|X_n−X|>ε)=P(a≠b)=1/2 for every n. — JUSTIFIED: Exactly two of the four equally likely points have unequal coordinates.
8. Therefore X_n does not converge to X in probability, and the proposed implication is false. — JUSTIFIED: The probability in Step 7 does not tend to 0, contradicting the required definition.
